headline: KSE-100 snaps its winning streak, sliding 1,733 points (−1.01%) to 170,498.94 on IMF-review caution and Middle East jitters, as Wall Street wobbles and the 10-year Treasury yield hits a fresh 19-year high on hawkish Fed signals while Brent tops $106 on the still-shut Strait of Hormuz
mood: Risk-off locally on profit-taking · yields and Hormuz keep the global tape fragile

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Snaps Winning Streak on Profit-Taking
five_things.html: The KSE-100 fell 1,733.57 points (−1.01%) on Thursday to close at 170,498.94, ending a three-session rally, after swinging between an intraday high of 172,491.16 and a low of 170,418.38. Volume eased to 759.97 million shares (from 773.59 million) but traded value rose to Rs27.54 billion (from Rs26.45 billion), as 358 stocks declined against just 101 advancers and 36 unchanged. Selling hit automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, E&P and OMC counters, with LUCK, HBL, MCB, MEBL, UBL, MARI, OGDC, PPL, PSO and SSGC among the index-heavy laggards; CNERGY (−3.3%), PACE and KOSM led percentage declines. Topline Securities said investors "moved to lock in profits, resulting in a broad-based retreat," with sentiment turning "fragile and risk-averse" on Middle East tensions and Brent crossing $100. Business Recorder and Profit confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Wobbles as Yields Climb
five_things.html: US equities were mixed-to-lower Thursday: the S&P 500 slipped 0.06% to 7,704.23, the Dow fell 0.31% to 51,349.89 and the Nasdaq dropped 1.1% to 26,936.04, pressured by the surging Treasury curve and crude's renewed advance even as hopes of a Hormuz de-escalation capped some of the losses. Yahoo Finance and TheStreet confirm the close.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to roughly 5.11-5.12%, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year climbed over 4bps to 4.94%, as Fed Governor Michael Barr said "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed," and President John Williams called another 2026 hike "reasonable." Odds of an October 27-28 hike jumped to roughly 70-77% on CME FedWatch, up sharply from the prior session, under Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish stance. CNBC and CNBC confirm the move.

five_things.chip: Oil Extends Rally as Hormuz Stays Shut
five_things.html: Brent rose 3.2% to $106.39 and WTI gained 2.8% to $94.76, up roughly 22% over the past month, as the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed to routine commercial shipping — IMF PortWatch recorded just 1 transit on 20 September against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. OPEC+'s Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee holds its 68th meeting on 4 October, though members' spare capacity to offset the shut-in Gulf barrels remains constrained. Trading Economics and The Conversation confirm.

five_things.chip: Gold and Silver Pull Back on Firmer Dollar
five_things.html: Gold eased to $4,273 (−0.3% / −$13.74 on the day) and silver fell 1.7% to $63.36, staying below $64/oz, as a firmer dollar and hawkish Fed repricing pressured precious metals even against the geopolitical backdrop. USAGOLD and Fortune confirm the pullback.
five_things.sentiment: pulling back on a firmer dollar

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's macro backdrop stays a study in contrasts: the KSE-100 snapped its rally, falling 1.01% to 170,498.94, as an IMF mission opened talks on the next EFF/RSF review and PM Shehbaz Sharif met Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on the sidelines of UNGA to reaffirm reform commitments. August CPI held at 11.15% y/y, well above the SBP's 5-7% target band, with food (+13.89%) and transport (+20.17%) the main drivers; the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at its 14 September MPC meeting, while 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.72/11.97% (bid/offer) as of 22 September. Separately, the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was deferred by the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, which is seeking a clause-by-clause justification before its next sitting. Profit and Business Recorder confirm.
matrix.gcc_html: The Gulf's non-oil economies keep outrunning the region's energy disruption: Saudi Arabia's PMI rose to a six-month high of 53.8 in August (from 53.1 in July), while the UAE's non-oil PMI jumped to 55.3 (from 52.7), its fastest pace since December 2024, even as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to routine shipping. Saudi's PIF continues rolling out its 2026-2030 strategy, with the Crown Prince launching CEER's flagship vehicles on 21 September and PIF-backed Tawrid and ASFAR's Gamra Mountain Resort both unveiled the prior week. OPEC+'s JMMC meets 4 October to review production policy against constrained Gulf spare capacity. Arab News and The National confirm.
matrix.global_html: The dominant global theme remains the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield's push to roughly 5.11-5.12%, a 19-year high, reflects Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish path, Governor Barr's and President Williams's comments flagging further tightening, and October rate-hike odds near 70-77% on CME FedWatch — a combination pressuring equities even as crude's advance adds an inflationary complication. Separately, Washington's tariff agenda widens on 29 September, when 100% Section 232 duties on patented pharmaceuticals extend to all importers beyond the 17 large companies already covered, alongside expanded Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods. CNBC and Wiley Trade Compliance confirm.

legislative.policy_html: Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — deferred by the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, which is seeking a clause-by-clause justification before its next sitting, as the IMF opens talks on the next EFF/RSF review
legislative.impact_html: Wins: institutional investors and IMF programme compliance, transparency advocates. Loses: SOE management facing tighter oversight, patronage-linked appointments.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+ Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee (68th meeting), 4 October 2026 — to review Gulf production policy as the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed to routine shipping and spare capacity remains constrained
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf producers still able to export via alternate routes, non-oil diversification plays (tourism, construction) on resilient PMIs. Loses: Kuwait and other export-constrained energy exporters absorbing Hormuz-linked shut-ins.

legislative.policy_html: Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs — 100% duty on patented pharmaceuticals extends to all remaining importers from 29 September 2026, alongside expanded Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods
legislative.sectors: Pharmaceuticals, healthcare supply chains, Canadian exporters
legislative.impact_html: Wins: US-based/onshoring pharma manufacturers with approved plans and MFN pricing deals (0% tariff until 2029), generics and biosimilars (exempt). Loses: mid-size branded importers without onshoring plans, Canadian exporters facing expanded Section 338 duties.

levels.resistance_note: first resistance; Thursday's intraday high of 172,491 above that

desk_stance_html: The desk reads Thursday's pullback as profit-taking after a three-session rally rather than a trend reversal, with breadth (358 decliners vs 101 advancers) reflecting broad-based de-risking ahead of the IMF's EFF/RSF review rather than a single catalyst. Global cross-currents — a 19-year-high 10-year yield, October Fed hike odds near 70-77%, and Brent above $106 on the still-shut Hormuz — argue for a cautious open, with energy-sensitive and rate-sensitive names likely to stay volatile. A close back above 171,700 would ease near-term pressure; a break below 169,500 opens room toward 168,700. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 snaps its rally — down 1,733 points (−1.01%) to 170,498.94 — as global yields hit a 19-year high and oil holds above $106 on the still-shut Strait of Hormuz.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities were mixed-to-lower Thursday: S&P 500 ▼0.06% to 7,704.23, Dow ▼0.31% to 51,349.89, Nasdaq ▼1.1% to 26,936.04. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to roughly 5.11-5.12%, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year rose to 4.94%, as Fed Governor Barr and President Williams flagged further tightening under Chair Kevin Warsh. October rate-hike odds jumped to 70-77% on CME FedWatch.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 1,733.57 points (−1.01%) to 170,498.94, ending a three-session rally, on broad-based selling (358 decliners vs 101 advancers) across autos, cement, banks, E&P and OMCs. Volume eased to 759.97m shares but value rose to Rs27.54bn. The pullback came as an IMF mission opened talks on the next EFF/RSF review and PM Shehbaz Sharif met MD Kristalina Georgieva at UNGA. August CPI held at 11.15% y/y (still above the SBP's 5-7% band); the SBP kept its policy rate at 11.5% on 14 September; 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.72/11.97%. The Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue deferred the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking a clause-by-clause justification.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's PMI rose to a six-month high of 53.8 in August (from 53.1); the UAE's non-oil PMI jumped to 55.3 (from 52.7), its fastest pace since December 2024 — both resilient despite the Strait of Hormuz remaining effectively closed to routine shipping (IMF PortWatch: 1 transit on 20 September vs an 85/day baseline). PIF continued rolling out its 2026-2030 strategy, with CEER's flagship vehicle launch on 21 September. OPEC+'s JMMC meets 4 October to review production policy.

GLOBAL
Brent rose 3.2% to $106.39 and WTI gained 2.8% to $94.76, up roughly 22% over the past month, on the ongoing Hormuz disruption. Gold eased 0.3% to $4,273 and silver fell 1.7% to $63.36 as a firmer dollar and hawkish Fed repricing pressured metals. Washington's tariff agenda widens 29 September: 100% Section 232 duties on patented pharmaceuticals extend to all remaining importers, alongside expanded Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
Pakistan: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill deferred in Senate committee — wins: institutional investors, IMF compliance; loses: SOE management facing tighter oversight.
GCC: OPEC+ JMMC meets 4 October amid Hormuz shut-ins — wins: non-oil diversification plays; loses: export-constrained Gulf energy exporters.
Global: Section 232/338 tariffs widen from 29 September — wins: onshoring pharma manufacturers, generics; loses: mid-size branded importers, Canadian exporters.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,500 (deeper support 168,700), pivot 170,499 (Thursday's close), resistance 171,700 (then Thursday's intraday high of 172,491). The desk reads Thursday's move as profit-taking after a three-session rally rather than a reversal, though a 19-year-high 10-year yield, surging October hike odds and Brent above $106 argue for a cautious open. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
